bbc.description: Parastoo Ahmadi, three musicians and a producer were reportedly given 74 lashes in Qom.

bbc.description: Interests of oil-producing countries, a US boycott and a dispute over finance may have torpedoed climate talks.

bbc.title: Israeli attacks have turned Gaza into 'toxic wasteland', Oxfam says
bbc.description: The report says there are signs of possible contamination across almost all of Gaza as a result of Israel's actions.

bbc.title: India pledges $1.6bn to Nepal in reset of ties
bbc.description: As Nepal rebuilds after deadly floods, its prime minister sets contentious issues aside to secure Indian funding, port access and a new train service.

bbc.title: Search and rescue teams race against time to find survivors after Nigeria boat tragedy
bbc.description: The government blames overcrowding, poor maintenance, and missing life jackets for boat accidents.

bbc.title: Prominent Zimbabwean preacher arrested on sexual assault allegations
bbc.description: Uebert Angel, a British-Zimbabwean national, leads a charismatic church with branches in several countries.

bbc.title: Comedian impersonates Trump's dance moves, mocks trade talks at Canada press dinner
bbc.description: The impersonator, Canadian comedian Mark Critch, poked fun at the US president's search for a new press secretary and US-Canada trade talks.

bbc.title: Flights cancelled in Belgium due to cost-of-living strike
bbc.description: A series of strikes have hit Belgium in recent months as the prime minister struggles to agree a budget to cut costs.

bbc.title: Mexican soldiers attacked in wake of drug lord's arrest
bbc.description: Eight suspects are arrested after firing on soldiers trying to re-establish order following the arrest of 'El Chapo Isidro'.

bbc.title: Miley Cyrus marries Maxx Morando in California ceremony
bbc.description: The couple have been together for four years and were engaged in 2025.

bbc.title: Kenya and DR Congo agree to restore ties after tensions over conflict
bbc.description: The two leaders committed to upholding sovereignty and "non-interference in the internal affairs of states".

bbc.title: Nigeria's president says he is also hit by water and power cuts plaguing country
bbc.description: Bola Tinubu says he was shaving last week when the water cut out - an experience familiar to many Nigerians.

bbc.title: Boy, 7, pulled alive from rubble hours after Russian strike on Ukraine, rescuers say
bbc.description: Eleven people are dead in the attack on Dymer, with rescue efforts ongoing to find those still missing from the residential building.

bbc.title: South Korea education minister resigns over exam cheating scandal
bbc.description: Choi Kyo-jin admits last-minute measures to stop AI-assisted cheating during the college entrance exam caused chaos.

bbc.title: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 after flipping North Carolina seat
bbc.description: Democrats have now won at least 258 seats in the midterms compared to Republicans, who hold at least 173 seats.

euronews.title: Visegrád Four leaders voice concerns over EU budget proposal
euronews.description: Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar said his government did not consider the proposal an acceptable starting point for negotiations.

euronews.title: Tanzania: Towering flames engulf beachfront hotels in Zanzibar
euronews.description: A massive fire swept through six beachfront hotels on the island of Zanzibar, Tanzania, on Saturday 21 November 2026, forcing around 180 tourists to evacuate as flames spread rapidly along the popular Nungwi Beach.

euronews.title: German-Ukrainian interceptor shoots down Russian jet-powered drone, company says
euronews.description: The GUR, Ukraine's military intelligence agency, said Russian forces began using the K5-K variant of the Geran-5 drone in attacks on Ukrainian cities at the beginning of autumn.

euronews.title: Belgium: Workers march against spending cuts as living costs rise
euronews.description: Thousands marched through Brussels, on Monday 23 November 2026, against proposed austerity measures, with some clashes prompting police to deploy tear gas and water cannons. The protests came as Belgium's government struggled to agree on its budget for 2027.

euronews.title: What went wrong at the COP31 climate talks? Europe Tonight breaks it down
euronews.description: Euronews' Felicia Pochhammer spoke to Chiara Martinelli, the director of Climate Action Network, to look at what went wrong at the COP31 climate talks and what it means for Europe and for the future of global climate action.

euronews.title: NATO warns of intensifying threats as Ukraine peace proposals face key questions
euronews.description: Henri Vanhanen, a senior fellow with the Transatlantic Security Initiative, joined Euronews’ new show Europe Tonight to discuss growing security concerns and the prospects for peace in Ukraine.

euronews.title: Merz says it was a 'mistake' not to admit Ukraine into NATO in 2008
euronews.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told reporters the Russian invasion of Ukraine would likely not have happened if allies had agreed to admit Kyiv in 2008 during a summit in Bucharest.

euronews.title: 'Don't waste those talents': GTA VI hacker released on licence
euronews.description: Arion Kurtaj managed to obtain 90 gameplay videos from Rockstar's much anticipated and at the time unfinished GTA VI game before leaking them online under the pseudonym "TeaPotUberHacker."

euronews.title: Iran carries out flogging of singer who performed without hijab
euronews.description: Ahmadi and four members of her concert team received lashes in Qom on Monday, her lawyer said, over a December 2024 performance, streamed live without an audience. A court sentenced nine team members to 74 lashes each, a two-year travel ban, and a two-year ban on artistic activity.

euronews.title: No, Greenland isn't being handed over to Trump. But what exactly has Washington secured?
euronews.description: The agreement builds on a 1951 defence agreement and comes after months of heightened tensions between Washington and the island under Danish sovereignty.

euronews.title: United Kingdom to host 2035 Women's World Cup, FIFA confirms
euronews.description: The chief executives of the English, Northern Irish, Scottish and Welsh football associations released a joint statement on Monday calling it a "landmark moment."

euronews.title: Von der Leyen and Kushner clash over peace talks sequence
euronews.description: Ursula von der Leyen and Jared Kushner cannot agree on when and how the issue of European security archicture should be discussed in the peace talks to end Russia's war on Ukraine.

euronews.title: Latest news bulletin | November 23rd, 2026 – Evening
euronews.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 23rd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

euronews.title: Europe Tonight: NATO security warnings, COP31 fallout, and Spain’s elections
euronews.description: NATO chief Mark Rutte warns of escalating hybrid threats as Ukraine pushes for membership, COP31 collapses without a climate deal, Spain faces a pivotal right-wing electoral shift, IG Metall workers strike across Germany, and Paris illuminates the Champs-Élysées for the holidays.

euronews.title: How artists from Qatar, Canada and Mexico are connecting cultures through creativity
euronews.description: Artists from Qatar, Mexico and Canada explore shared traditions, personal histories and new creative connections through the 2026 Year of Culture.

euronews.title: Dutch court bans BYD model from EU over likeness to Land Rover's Defender
euronews.description: The Chinese carmaker plans to appeal, and the ruling doesn't stop the car going on sale in Britain in January.

euronews.title: Macron announces €350 million research aid for France's aeronautics industry
euronews.description: During a visit to the Airbus site in Blagnac near Toulouse, the French president announced 350 million euros in state support for aeronautics research and innovation, plus special industrial zones to ease new factory projects.

euronews.title: AI just cracked the biggest maths problem of all time: what does it mean?
euronews.description: Some wonder if the solving of the famous Riemann Hypothesis by Anthropic’s Claude model is the beginning of advanced super intelligence.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, Jensen Huang réintégré chez Nvidia à la surprise générale : le dirigeant accueilli sous les applaudissements de centaines de salariés ; Wall Street clôture en très forte hausse
lemonde.description: Le conseil d’administration de Nvidia a annoncé lundi la réintégration immédiate de Jensen Huang comme directeur général et président du géant américain des puces, dix jours après sa démission liée à un scandale mêlant adultère, espionnage et contrebande. Plusieurs parlementaires, démocrates et républicains, réclament des explications.

lemonde.title: Deux navires russes attaqués dans les eaux libyennes, une extension inédite de la guerre russo-ukrainienne
lemonde.description: Le président ukrainien, Volodymyr Zelensky, a revendiqué, lundi 23 novembre, le double assaut mené la veille par « sept drones navals » dans la zone maritime de Benghazi. Une telle attaque contre des bateaux russes transportant de l’armement permet à Kiev de montrer que ses forces sont en mesure de frapper les intérêts de Moscou où qu’ils se trouvent.

lemonde.title: La France va créer des stocks stratégiques de terres rares et de métaux prioritaires pour réduire sa dépendance à la Chine d’ici à 2027
lemonde.description: La Caisse des dépôts, qui pilotera le projet, va consulter les industriels des secteurs stratégiques utilisant ces matières premières.

lemonde.title: Le prix de L’Equerre d’argent distingue la restructuration du Musée des arts décoratifs et du design de Bordeaux
lemonde.description: Le jury de cette 44ᵉ édition a récompensé, lundi, le projet réalisé par l’agence Antoine Dufour pour le soin apporté aux détails, la grande finesse du dessin et la maîtrise de toutes les dimensions du processus de transformation.

lemonde.title: Retraites : la Cour des comptes plaide pour une limitation des possibilités de départs anticipés
lemonde.description: Dans une note diffusée lundi, la haute juridiction formule plusieurs pistes pour garantir la soutenabilité financière du système par répartition. L’une d’elles recommande de revoir les dispositifs grâce auxquels près d’un assuré sur deux peut toucher sa pension avant l’âge légal.

lemonde.title: La testostérone, hormone de tous les fantasmes : enquête sur ses effets réels et supposés sur la virilité, la force physique ou l’agressivité
lemonde.description: Prisée par l’administration Trump et les masculinistes, cette molécule n’est pas seulement une hormone sexuelle. Son rôle est bien plus subtil – et parfois paradoxal – que l’image qui en est véhiculée. Enquête sur les mythes qui entourent C₁₉H₂₈O₂.

lemonde.title: Budget 2027 : Sébastien Lecornu appelle au « compromis » dans une lettre aux parlementaires et liste les priorités du gouvernement
lemonde.description: Alors que les projets de loi de finances et de financement de la Sécurité sociale ont été rejetés à l’Assemblée nationale, le premier ministre souhaite poursuivre les discussions avec les parlementaires.

lemonde.title: Budget : ces cinq obstacles auxquels se heurte le projet d’inscrire une « règle d’or » dans la Constitution
lemonde.description: Impopularité d’Emmanuel Macron, calendrier restreint, complexité technique, efficacité aléatoire, rigidité… La méthode annoncée par le chef de l’Etat pour imposer le retour à l’équilibre budgétaire nécessite de surmonter de fortes difficultés.

lemonde.title: Une enquête ouverte dans une école de police de Seine-et-Marne après des accusations de racisme, de salut nazi et d’agression sexuelle
lemonde.description: La justice a été saisie le 29 octobre par le commandant de l’établissement situé à Cannes-Ecluse, sur la base de l’article 40 du code de procédure pénale, qui oblige les agents publics à signaler d’éventuelles infractions pénales.

lemonde.title: A Paris, les conflits autour de l’espace public pourraient faire le bonheur du secteur privé
lemonde.description: Avec le recul de l’automobile, un mouvement important de mixité des usages sur la chaussée s’est imposé au cours de la dernière décennie dans la capitale. La mairie n’a pas les moyens de réguler seule ce nouvel afflux et les frictions qu’il engendre.

lemonde.title: L’Union européenne veut « interdire l’affichage des symboles russes » dans les compétitions sportives sur son sol
lemonde.description: La Commission européenne n’entend pas laisser les athlètes russes concourir sous leurs couleurs. Elle souhaite aussi interdire « aux Européens de continuer à occuper des postes dans les instances dirigeantes des entreprises en Russie ».

lemonde.title: Grand Paris Express : l’ouverture de la nouvelle ligne 18 du métro plus compromise que jamais
lemonde.description: Valérie Pécresse, présidente de la région Ile-de-France, a convoqué une réunion d’urgence avec les acteurs concernés et enjoint Alstom, concepteur du système d’automatisation, à trouver « des solutions pour fiabiliser son logiciel ».

lemonde.title: Au Soudan, tensions internationales accrues après une frappe de drone contre un bâtiment de l’ONU
lemonde.description: L’armée de Khartoum accuse les paramilitaires des Forces de soutien rapide d’avoir lancé leur offensive aérienne à partir du territoire éthiopien.

lemonde.title: Glyphosate : la cancérogénicité de l’herbicide de Bayer reconnue par une institution scientifique majeure aux Etats-Unis
lemonde.description: L’Institut de recherche fédéral sur la santé environnementale a publié, vendredi, une large réévaluation de la cancérogénicité du glyphosate. Un document sans conséquence à ce stade sur les contraintes réglementaires encadrant l’herbicide outre-Atlantique.

lemonde.title: Les Etats-Unis annoncent de nouvelles sanctions pour priver l’Iran de rentrées d’argent
lemonde.description: Des milliards de dollars de transactions suspectes liées à l’Iran ont été détectés par le régulateur américain FinCEN entre 2025 et 2026, selon le Trésor.

lemonde.title: La cicatrice de Patricia, 33 ans : « Je deviens la cible de moqueries, on me surnomme Ribéry à l’école »
lemonde.description: « Dans la peau ». On a tous des cicatrices. Stigmates d’une chute, d’un accident, d’une maladie. Même refermées, ces blessures font désormais partie de notre identité. Un berger allemand a déchiré la peau de la joue de Patricia, quand elle avait 3 ans.

rfi.title: Macron pledges €350m for aviation research, pushes industrial acceleration
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has announced €350 million in funding for civil aviation research, and plans to create new industrial zones with simplified administrative procedures, as France looks to accelerate its reindustrialisation. The announcement came during the second Choose France business summit focused on the home market.

rfi.title: Zelensky calls for EU inclusion in talks with Russia 'as soon as possible'
rfi.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday called for new negotiations with Russia involving European leaders to be held as soon as possible and repeated a plea for his country to join the NATO alliance.

rfi.title: UN condemns drone strikes in Khartoum suspected to have come from Ethiopia
rfi.description: A United Nations building was one of several structures damaged in drone attacks on Sudan’s capital, Khartoum, which are suspected to have been launched from Ethiopia.

rfi.title: Major cyberattack hits IT systems at Guadeloupe university hospital
rfi.description: A major cyberattack has disrupted the university hospital in the French overseas department of Guadeloupe, affecting its operations and forcing it to activate its emergency response plan and postponing non-emergency procedures.

rfi.title: French pair target Grand Slam glory after ATP Finals crown in Turin
rfi.description: French tennis players Théo Arribagé and Albano Olivetti were on Monday setting their sights on playing in their country's Davis Cup team and trophies at the four Grand Slam tournaments next year after capturing the doubles title at the 2026 men's end-of-season championships.

rfi.title: France seeks fresh start with Israel as Lebanon peacekeeping deadline looms
rfi.description: France is hoping to rebuild relations with Israel's next government as it steps up efforts to secure a new security arrangement for southern Lebanon before the United Nations peacekeeping mission there ends its operations in December.

rfi.title: UN warns Libya must not become stage for Russia-Ukraine war after drone strikes
rfi.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday said his country was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya, adding that one of them sank in the latest spillover from Moscow's war with Kyiv. The United Nations condemned Sunday's strikes and has called for an international investigation.

rfi.title: Cop31 climate talks collapse as EU rejects deal that omits fossil fuels
rfi.description: The Cop31 climate summit in Turkey has ended in disarray after the European Union and several other countries rejected a proposed global agreement that failed to explicitly mention fossil fuels. The breakdown, after more than two weeks of negotiations and a record 44 hours of overtime, marks a major setback for international climate diplomacy, with deep divisions over energy policy and financial support for developing nations left unresolved.

rfi.title: French right backs Macron's plan to put public spending limits in Constitution
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron is reportedly considering a constitutional reform to curb public deficits, with right-wing parties and the far-right National Rally signalling their willingness to support the move. The proposal could bring MPs and senators together for a vote as early as January, just months before the 2027 presidential election.

rfi.title: EU proposes digital tax to fund budget as France and Germany clash over cuts
rfi.description: The European Union has unveiled plans to tax the world's biggest digital companies to help finance its next long-term budget, as Brussels seeks to overcome deep divisions between member states over spending priorities. The proposal has already drawn criticism from France and Germany, highlighting the challenge of securing an agreement before the end of the year.

rfi.title: Nepal's first climate loss and damage payout falls far short of needs
rfi.description: Nepal is set to become the first country to receive money from the UN's Loss and Damage Fund following devastating floods in August. But the provisional €19 million allocation covers less than 1 percent of the damage – and survivors are still waiting for help.

rfi.title: Traditional French tapestry captures fantastical world of Japanese anime
rfi.description: The French town of Aubusson is renowned for producing some of the world's finest tapestries. Now its weavers are using centuries-old techniques to reimagine scenes from the fantastical films of Japanese animators Studio Ghibli – and unearthing some unexpected connections in the process.

rfi.title: National Assembly backs greater legal protection for police using firearms
rfi.description: France's parliament has approved legislation giving police officers greater legal protection when using their firearms, prompting fierce criticism from rights groups who warn it could make it harder to investigate alleged police brutality. The government insists the measure is needed to protect officers carrying out increasingly demanding duties.

rfi.title: French court finds racism played role in police beating of black music producer
rfi.description: A French court has handed down prison sentences to three police officers for the violent assault of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020, ruling that racism was an aggravating factor in a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police brutality and racial discrimination.

rfi.title: Former PM de Villepin launches 2027 presidential bid with warning to far right
rfi.description: Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin has announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election, promising to restore France's international influence, tackle growing inequality and challenge the rise of the far right. The veteran conservative also delivered a blistering assessment of President Emmanuel Macron's leadership, accusing him of allowing the country's political and social divisions to deepen.

rfi.title: France must change or 'risk losing' overseas territories, former PM tells RFI
rfi.description: France's territories outside Europe are a major strategic asset, giving it a foothold on five continents and in three oceans. Yet Paris has long been accused of neglecting the nearly 3 million people living outside mainland France, who face deep economic and social inequalities. With calls for independence growing, former prime minister Manuel Valls warns that France risks losing its overseas territories unless it radically changes its relationship with them.

rfi.title: Students and unions unite for sixth weekend of protests across France
rfi.description: Thousands of demonstrators took to the streets across France on Saturday for a sixth consecutive weekend of protests against rising living costs, deteriorating public services and growing inequality. The movement, which began with student demonstrations in September, has since broadened into a nationwide campaign and inspired similar rallies elsewhere in Europe.

rfi.title: Turkey seizes control of last major independent news channel amid fraud scandal
rfi.description: Turkey's last operating independent TV news channel has fallen under state control, as President Recep Tayyip Erdogan scrambles to contain a wave of public fury over a $20 billion investment fund scandal that has swallowed the life savings of hundreds of thousands of people in the country.

france24fr.title: Megaspeed, société singapourienne au cœur du scandale Nvidia, placée sur liste noire américaine
france24fr.description: Le ministère du Commerce américain a décidé lundi de placer sur liste noire la société singapourienne Megaspeed et ses filiales, suspectées d'avoir contourné l'embargo des États-Unis en fournissant des puces Nvidia à la Chine.

france24fr.title: Le chef de l'ONU espère voir d'ici un an un mécanisme pour limiter les risques posés par l'IA
france24fr.description: Antonio Guterres a appelé lundi les États membres des Nations unies à élaborer, "d'ici l'année prochaine, un cadre multilatéral de gestion des risques liés à l'IA". Pour le chef de l'ONU, la première étape pourrait être de convenir de mesures de sécurité communes, d'un système d'évaluation et d'exigences minimales en matière de contrôle indépendant.

france24fr.title: Génocide des Rohingya en Birmanie : 14 pays reconnaissent la décision de la CIJ
france24fr.description: Le Royaume-Uni, l'Espagne, le Canada, l'Australie et dix autres pays ont affirmé lundi reconnaître la décision de la Cour internationale de justice, qui a reconnu la semaine dernière le génocide commis par la Birmanie contre les Rohingya. Ils exhortent la Birmanie à se "conformer pleinement à ses obligations en vertu du droit international, y compris à la décision de la Cour".

france24fr.title: RD Congo : une messe interdite, tensions entre l'Eglise et les autorités
france24fr.description: L'Eglise catholique est-elle dans le viseur des autorités congolaises ? Ces derniers jours elles ont empêché deux évènements : une marche à Lubumbashi et une messe à Kinshasa. Dans le même temps en République démocratique du Congo, on attend toujours la nomination du comité d'organisation du dialogue national. Les précisions de notre correspondante Aurélie Bazzara-Kibangula.

france24fr.title: Terres rares : Emmanuel Macron annonce que la France va se doter de "stocks stratégiques"
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron a annoncé un projet pour pourvoir la France de "stocks stratégiques" de minerais critiques, a déclaré l'Élysée lundi. Le programme inspiré des réserves stratégiques de pétrole aura pour but de sécuriser l'approvisionnement en terres rares et en "certains métaux prioritaires" et de réduire la dépendance vis-à-vis de la Chine.

france24fr.title: L'attaque ukrainienne à Benghazi attise les tensions en Libye et en Méditerranée
france24fr.description: À la suite de l'attaque ukrainienne contre un navire de guerre russe à Benghazi, des publications sur les réseaux sociaux détournent d'anciennes vidéos pour illustrer les événements. Elles ont été prises en Grèce il y a plusieurs mois. Par ailleurs, une question revient sur les réseaux sociaux : d'où sont partis les drones marins utilisés pour l'attaque ? Les accusations fusent et ravivent les tensions entre les rivaux de l'ouest et de l'est de la Libye. Jules BOITEAU dans Info Intox.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle : qui pourra rassembler ?
france24fr.description: À moins de cinq mois du premier tour de la présidentielle, prévu le 18 avril, la course à l’Élysée s’annonce particulièrement disputée. Dernier en date à entrer dans la course : Dominique de Villepin, qui a officialisé sa candidature vendredi. Plusieurs candidats de la droite et du centre veulent s’affronter dans une primaire afin de désigner un seul représentant, mais l’idée ne fait pas l’unanimité. David Lisnard, qui est en progression dans les sondages, entend peser dans les discussions et po

france24fr.title: "Notre avenir plutôt que leurs guerres" : en Europe, la jeunesse se mobilise contre le réarmement
france24fr.description: Berlin, Paris, Madrid, Milan, Vienne... Depuis vendredi, partout en Europe, des centaines de milliers de jeunes manifestent autour de deux mots d'ordre : pour l'avenir de la jeunesse, contre la vie chère. Ils dénoncent notamment la hausse des budgets militaires qui, selon eux, se fait au détriment de l'éducation, du climat et des services publics.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : le pétrole tient-il ses promesses depuis le premier baril en 2024 ?
france24fr.description: 🇸🇳 Deux ans après le premier baril de pétrole de Sangomar, le Sénégal peine encore à transformer ses ressources énergétiques en bénéfices pour sa population. Entre cherté du gaz domestique et une année marquée par des coupures d'électricité pendant l'été, le ministre de l'Energie et du pétrole reste optimiste.

france24fr.title: Échec de la COP31 : et maintenant ?
france24fr.description:
La COP31 s’est achevée sans accord sur la sortie des énergies fossiles ni avancée majeure sur le financement climatique. Un nouvel échec pour la diplomatie climatique, alors que le réchauffement s’accélère. Les COP peuvent-elles encore faire avancer la lutte contre le changement climatique ?
 
Laurence Tubiana, présidente de la Fondation européenne pour le climat et ancienne négociatrice de l’Accord de Paris, analyse les conséquences de ce sommet.

france24fr.title: Navires russes ciblés en Libye : l'Ukraine étend le domaine de la lutte
france24fr.description: Le président Volodymyr Zelensky a revendiqué lundi l'attaque de deux navires russes au large de Benghazi, dans l'est de la Libye. Une opération spectaculaire destinée à frapper la logistique russe et remettre le dossier ukrainien au cœur des préoccupations internationales.

france24fr.title: Football : l'Afrique soutient la réélection de Gianni Infantino à la tête de la FIFA
france24fr.description: ⚽ La CAF affiche son soutien à Gianni Infantino pour un nouveau mandat à la tête de la FIFA. L’annonce a été faite par Patrice Motsepe, président de l'instance du football africain, lors de sa 48e assemblée générale ordinaire, samedi à Abuja au Nigéria.

france24fr.title: Après l'échec de la COP31, quel avenir pour la diplomatie climatique?
france24fr.description: La COP31 s'est achevée sans accord final. Les pays producteurs de pétrole ont fait pression pour que la sortie des énergies fossiles ne soit pas mentionnée dans la déclaration. Plus d'une centaine de pays se sont en conséquence opposé à son adoption sans cette mention. Cette COP était la première depuis l'annonce par l'ONU du dépassement "inévitable" d'1,5°C de réchauffement climatique. "Le monde ne peut pas se permettre que cela se reproduise", a jugé le chef de l'ONU Climat, Simon Stiell.

france24fr.title: Belgique : le pays en grève  contre l’austérité  du gouvernement
france24fr.description: Alors que des dizaines de milliers de Belges protestaient contre l'austérité ce lundi 23 novembre, le roi Philippe a accordé un délai supplémentaire à Bart De Wever pour tenter de débloquer les négociations budgétaires. Le Premier ministre s'est donné jusqu'à la fin de l'année pour trouver un accord au sein de sa coalition, faute de quoi ce sera la fin de son gouvernement.

france24fr.title: Jensen Huang de retour à la tête de Nvidia dans un volte-face inattendu
france24fr.description: Le conseil d'administration de Nvidia a annoncé lundi la réintégration immédiate de Jensen Huang comme patron du géant américain des puces électroniques, sur fond de pression de Donald Trump, malgré un scandale mêlant adultère, espionnage et contrebande.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Nvidia : les démocrates assurent que l'administration Trump et Jensen Huang feront l'objet d'enquêtes approfondies
Nvidia : Jensen Huang retrouve ses fonctions de directeur général
france24fr.description: Nvidia a annoncé ⁠lundi que Jensen Huang ​reprenait avec effet immédiat son poste de directeur général de l'entreprise, spécialisée dans les puces pour intelligence artificielle, 11 jours après sa démission suite à la révélation de relations extraconjugales, dont l'une avec ​une espionne chinoise présumée.

france24fr.title: Égypte : le désert de Fayoum, trésor astral méconnu
france24fr.description: Situé à environ 100 km au sud-ouest du Caire, le désert de Fayoum offre un ciel nocturne d'une grande pureté, loin de la pollution lumineuse des grandes villes, ce qui en fait un spot privilégié pour l'observation des étoiles et l'astrophotographie.

zeit.title: Ukraine-Krieg: Luftalarm in Polen - Anwohner sollen Schutzräume aufsuchen
Fernsehen: Nach Ausfall Nuhrs: ARD plant keinen Satire-Jahresrückblick
Wogen geglättet?: Landeschef Schnieder: «Der Streit und Zank müssen aufhören»
Verkehr: 22 Park-and-Ride-Anlagen fallen im ADAC-Test durch
Staatsschutz ermittelt: Unbekannter soll Grünen-Sitzung in Schwerte gestürmt haben
Polizei ermittelt: Einbrecher stiehlt Bargeld aus Kindergarten
Unfälle: Ein Toter und ein Schwerverletzter bei Frontalzusammenstoß
Brexit-Debatte: Andy Burnham verteidigt Annäherung an die EU im britischen Parlament
zeit.description: Der britische Premier setzt sich für eine engere Zusammenarbeit zwischen EU und Großbritannien ein. Eine Abkehr vom Brexit könnte die Wirtschaft ankurbeln, sagt er.

zeit.title: Jensen Huang: Ein krasser Powermove (5/5)
zeit.description: Jensen Huang kehrt zurück an die Spitze von Nvidia. Die Börse feiert, der US-Präsident ist hocherfreut. Doch viele Fragen bleiben offen.

zeit.title: Parastoo Ahmadi: Bekannte iranische Sängerin nach Konzert mit 74 Hieben ausgepeitscht
zeit.description: Weil sie bei einem Konzert gegen die Bekleidungsregeln im Iran verstieß, wurde Parastoo Ahmadi mit Dutzenden Hieben ausgepeitscht. Menschenrechtler äußern sich entsetzt.

zeit.title: Jensen Huang: Jensen Huang hätte nie zurückkehren dürfen. Aber es ging nicht anders
zeit.description: Wenn irgendjemand noch Zweifel hatte, wie in der Tech-Branche geherrscht wird: bitte sehr. Das Silicon Valley braucht seine Lichtgestalten eben mehr als jede Moral.

zeit.title: Drohnenangriff auf die »Sparta II«: Boris Pistorius warnt vor Ausweitung des Ukrainekriegs auf die Ostsee
zeit.description: Der Verteidigungsminister zeigt sich besorgt über die Angriffe auf ein russisches Schiff vor der Küste Finnlands. Auch die Ukraine habe eine Verantwortung.

zeit.title: Anschlag auf den CSD: Mein arabisches Coming-out
zeit.description: Unser Autor ist schwul, Araber, und trat auf dem Berliner CSD auf, bevor das Attentat geschah. Seitdem ist sie wieder da – eine alte Angst, die er neu überwinden muss.

zeit.title: Krieg gegen die Ukraine: Nato verstärkt Kontrolle von Polens Luftraum
zeit.description: Nach dem Absturz russischer Marschflugkörper sind Aufklärungsflugzeuge der Nato über Polen im Einsatz. Finnland bestellt Russlands Botschafter ein. Das Liveblog

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Revolutionswächter melden brennende Tanker in Hormuz +++ Bahrain gerät erneut unter iranischen Beschuss
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Nvidia macht eine abrupte Kehrtwende und holt Jensen Huang als CEO zurück
nzz.description: Der Verwaltungsrat des Chip-Entwicklers spricht sich einstimmig für die Rückkehr des Langzeitchefs aus, der das Unternehmen wegen mehrerer Affären verlassen musste.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Spionageaffäre bei Nvidia: Jensen Huang sagt: «Ich werde beim zweiten Mal ein besserer Chef sein» +++ Megaspeed steht in den USA neu auf schwarzer Liste
nzz.description: Der Nvidia-Chef Jensen Huang hatte mutmasslich eine Affäre mit einer chinesischen Spionin. Als Berichte über weitere Liaisons publik wurden, trat er von seinem Posten zurück. Die neuesten Entwicklungen zum Fall.

nzz.title: Die Fussball-Weltmeisterschaft der Frauen findet 2031 unter anderem in den USA statt
nzz.description: Die Vereinigten Staaten werden in fünf Jahren gemeinsam mit Mexiko, Costa Rica und Jamaika die Organisation der WM übernehmen.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN KULTUR - Elias Hirschl gewinnt den österreichischen Buchpreis +++ Kabarettist Dieter Nuhr an Krebs erkrankt
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus dem Feuilleton.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Fifa-Präsidium: Infantino wollte offenbar Rechte an der Weltmeisterschaft für 96 Jahre an private Investoren abgeben
nzz.description: Nach der WM im Sommer 2026 ist der Kampf um das Fifa-Präsidium entbrannt. Im März findet die Wahl des Präsidenten statt. Die jüngsten Entwicklungen und die Hintergründe im Überblick.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Polen bestellt nach Raketenabstürzen den russischen Botschafter ein +++ Merz warnt Russland vor weiteren «Provokationen»
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Russland plant offenbar die Stationierung einer Atomwaffe im All
nzz.description: Westliche Geheimdienste gehen laut Medienberichten davon aus, dass Moskau einen Satellit bereithält – und diesen innert zweier Monate mit Atomladung ins All schicken könnte.

nzz.title: Fanta, Ragusa und «Falscher Hase»: Wie Kriege unsere Küche prägten
nzz.description: In Iran kosten Eier, Poulet und Reis heute bis zu vierzigmal so viel wie vor sechs Jahren. Wenn im Krieg die Vorräte schrumpfen, erfinden Haushalte Notlösungen. Einige davon blieben bis heute.

nzz.title: Auto- und Velofreunde machen gemeinsame Sache gegen das neue Zürcher Tram
nzz.description: Das Kantonsparlament spricht Millionen für das Tram Affoltern. Doch wenn es zum Referendum kommt, könnte die SVP den Stadt-Land-Graben beackern – und auf Unterstützung von links zählen.

nzz.title: EU-Kommission will Russland-Flagge an Sportveranstaltungen verbieten
nzz.description: Ein Vorschlag der Kommission sieht vor, dass russische Sportlerinnen und Sportler bei Wettkämpfen in der EU künftig nicht mehr für ihr Land antreten dürfen. Russischen Soldaten soll die Einreise ganz verwehrt werden.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Trump macht Putin und Xi einen Gefallen – nicht Amerika
nzz.description: Der Dreiergipfel mit Xi und Putin in China zeigt klar: Trump hat nichts aus der schweren Niederlage seiner Partei bei den Midterms gelernt. Im Weissen Haus sitzt ein unbelehrbarer Präsident, der die Interessen von Autokraten über jene Amerikas und der freien Welt stellt.

nzz.title: Platzt jetzt die KI-Blase – oder bietet sich eine Kaufgelegenheit?
nzz.description: Die grossen Investitionen im Technologiesektor, hohe Schulden und steigende Zinsen haben für Unruhe an den Finanzmärkten gesorgt. Gleichwohl spricht einiges für eine Erholung zum Jahresende.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - Profitiert Genf von Kriegen? Nein, sagt die Wirtschaftsministerin des Kantons und fordert: «Wir müssen dem Rohstoffhandel Sorge tragen»
nzz.description: Die boomende Branche hat Genf zum grössten Beitragszahler im Finanzausgleich gemacht. Delphine Bachmann erklärt, warum der Kanton sich trotzdem verschuldet – und was Zürich besser macht.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN POLIZEI - Zwei Diebe beklauen Zugreisenden – dieser hilft, sie am Zürcher Hauptbahnhof festzunehmen
nzz.description: Die neuesten Polizeimeldungen aus der Schweiz.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN WIRTSCHAFT - Micasa-CEO kündigt seinen Rücktritt an +++ ABB will deutschen Ventilatorenhersteller Ziehl-Abegg übernehmen
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus der Wirtschaft.

observador.title: Jornalista Sofia Craveiro vence prémio Euro-Mediterrânico
observador.description: O prémio foi atribuído pela reportagem "As Gastarbeiterinnen portuguesas da Alemanha não querem voltar" publicada em janeiro no jornal Público que foi selecionada entre mais de 200 candidaturas.

observador.title: Detido em Loures com 42 armas para transformação
observador.description: O suspeito, de 61 anos, convertia armas de alarme em armas de disparo e afinava mecanismos de tiro para clientes. Ficou em prisão preventiva após interrogatório judicial.

observador.title: Parlamento distingue saúde mental e refugiados ucranianos
observador.description: Associação para o Estudo e Integração Psicossociais (AEIPS) e a HELP UA/Ukrainian Refugees UAPT vão receber o Prémio Direitos Humanos 2026 da Assembleia da República a 10 de dezembro.

observador.title: Governo açoriano realça melhoria "histórica" na Educação
observador.description: A secretária da Educação afirmou que a região melhorou nos resultados das provas PISA em relação ao país e até à média da OCDE e destacou que em 14 disciplinas oito estiveram acima da média nacional.

observador.title: Torres Novas celebra Natal com música, teatro e feira
observador.description: As festividades arrancam esta sexta-feira na Praça 5 de Outubro e prolongam-se até 11 de janeiro. A campanha de incentivo ao comércio local esgotou em uma semana em 2025.

observador.title: Faro aprova orçamento de 72 milhões de euros para 2027
observador.description: Orçamento previsional para o próximo ano é inferior em 11,5 milhões de euros relativamente ao de 2026, representando uma redução na ordem dos 13,7%, terá ainda de ser submetido à Assembleia Municipal.

observador.title: Nova coleção recupera vidas de atrizes portuguesas
observador.description: O D. Maria II lança no sábado a coleção "Biografias do Teatro Português: Mulheres", com seis volumes sobre figuras femininas entre os séculos XVIII e XX. O primeiro retrata Carlota Talassi.

observador.title: Rússia vai rejeitar novo acordo de cereais
observador.description: A representante permanente adjunta russa nas Nações Unidas acusa os aliados de Kiev de usarem o entendimento para exportar armas para a Ucrânia.

observador.title: Merz: foi “erro” NATO ter rejeitado adesão da Ucrânia
observador.description: Friedrich Merz considera que se a Ucrânia se tivesse tornado membro da NATO, a guerra provavelmente teria sido prevenida.

observador.title: BYD prepara um concorrente do Smart #2 mas mais futurista
observador.description: O maior construtor chinês continua a crescer de forma imparável. Depois de lançar o  Yangwang U9 Extreme com 3.039 cv, prepara-se para conceber um concorrente do Smart #2. E já registou o modelo.

observador.title: Os detalhes da acusação no abandono das crianças francesas
observador.description: Despacho de acusação do DIAP de Grândola detalha dias de violência sobre os dois irmãos, o estratagema do "jogo" para os abandonar numa floresta e a fuga dos arguidos até Fátima, onde foram detidos.

observador.title: Lisboa quer instalar 68 câmaras de videovigilância na Baixa
observador.description: Joana Baptista considera ser de "importância máxima à instalação do sistema de videovigilância no Martim Moniz e na Mouraria", face aos  "recentes episódios de violência no espaço público".

observador.title: O futuro da criatividade das marcas está nas mãos dos cri...
observador.description: Os criadores de conteúdo estão a mudar as regras da criatividade das marcas. Mas estarão a substituir as agências? Ana Roma Torres, da Havas Play, reflete sobre esta nova realidade.

observador.title: Fesap envia carta a Montenegro a exigir respostas
observador.description: O secretário-geral da Fesap, José Abraão, anunciou uma carta ao primeiro-ministro e uma reunião suplementar para acelerar as negociações sobre salários e carreiras na função pública.

observador.title: Estabilizar encosta de Manteigas "não é fácil e vai demorar"
observador.description: Maria da Graça Carvalho visitou a Mata da Carvalheira, origem do deslizamento de 18 de novembro. Intervenção pode custar entre 10 e 20 milhões de euros, sem prazo definido.

observador.title: Porto prevê orçamento de 510 milhões de euros para 2027
observador.description: O documento vai a votos na reunião de executivo de quinta-feira. Habitação lidera as dotações com 53 milhões, mobilidade leva 50 milhões e segurança recebe 17 milhões de euros.

observador.title: 22h. Ventura nega aliança com PS e discorda de Passos Coelho
observador.description: O líder do Chega reiterou o voto contra na votação final global do OE e fala também em vitimização por parte do governo. Ainda, Futebol Clube do Porto joga amanhã frente ao Feyenoord.

observador.title: Qual era o real plano de Infantino para "vender" Mundial
observador.description: The Guardian e The Athletic tiveram acesso a documentos para criação da FIFA Forward Entreprise feitos na véspera da final entre Espanha e Argentina que explicam projeto. Quando se "soube", tudo caiu.

spiegel.title: Türkei: Löwenalarm in Istanbul – Behörden geben nach Sichtung Entwarnung
spiegel.description: Ein vermeintlicher Löwe versetzt Istanbul in Aufregung. Nach der Auswertung neuer Aufnahmen gibt es jedoch Entwarnung. Welches Tier den Alarm ausgelöst hat, bleibt aber rätselhaft.

spiegel.title: Künstliche Intelligenz: António Guterres fordert globalen Pakt gegen KI-Risiken
spiegel.description: UN-Generalsekretär António Guterres dringt auf eine globale Vereinbarung zum Umgang mit den Risiken künstlicher Intelligenz. Innerhalb eines Jahres sollen sich die Staaten einigen.

spiegel.title: Nato verstärkt Kontrolle von Polens Luftraum - verlegt Awacs-Frühwarnflugzeug
spiegel.description: Drei russische Marschflugkörper sind nach einem Eindringen in den polnischen Luftraum abgestürzt. Die Nato reagiert nun mit zusätzlicher Überwachung – und prüft weitere Schritte.

spiegel.title: Ann-Katrin Berger: Nationaltorhüterin wechselt vom US-Club Gotham FC zu Union Berlin
spiegel.description: Von Chelsea über New York nach Köpenick: Union Berlin holt eine der prominentesten deutschen Fußballerinnen in die Bundesliga. Für den Club ist das ein Meilenstein, für Berger offenbar Ehrensache.

spiegel.title: Nvidia: Jensen Huang kehrt auf Druck von Donald Trump zurück
spiegel.description: Der zurückgetretene Nvidia-CEO kommt auf Trumps Druck zurück. Das zeigt: Wenn man nur genug Börsenwert kreiert und in der richtigen Technologie unterwegs ist, gelten nicht die gleichen Regeln.

spiegel.title: Jared Kushner: Donald Trumps Schwiegersohn und Chefvermittler wird immer reicher
spiegel.description: Jared Kushner verhandelt für das Weiße Haus in aller Welt. Doch in der Ukraine, in Gaza und im Irankrieg war er bisher erfolglos. Eines aber gelingt dem Chefgesandten Trumps prächtig – Reichtum anzuhäufen.

spiegel.title: Iran: Sängerin Parastu Ahmadi wegen Verstoß gegen Kopftuchpflicht ausgepeitscht
spiegel.description: Laut einem Medienbericht ist die iranische Sängerin Parastu Ahmadi ausgepeitscht worden. Sie hatte ohne Kopftuch gesungen und damit gegen iranische Gesetze verstoßen. Menschenrechtler kritisieren die Strafe scharf.

spiegel.title: Jamal Musiala: Experte widerspricht Hoeneß und Rummenigge im Gehaltsstreit
spiegel.description: Der an Absencen leidende Jamal Musiala soll auf Gehalt verzichten. Das fordern Uli Hoeneß und Karl-Heinz Rummenigge. Im SPIEGEL widersprechen Experten der Darstellung der Bayern-Funktionäre. Was ist deren Ziel?

spiegel.title: BYD: Aktie fällt nach EU-Verkaufsverbot für Ti7-SUV wegen Defender-Ähnlichkeit
spiegel.description: BYD hat ein Verkaufsverbot für seinen SUV Ti7 in der EU erhalten. Das Modell sehe dem Land Rover Defender zu ähnlich, so das Gericht. Die Aktie des chinesischen Autobauers fällt, er kündigt rechtliche Gegenwehr an.

spiegel.title: Femizide sollen als Mord statt als Totschlag gelten
spiegel.description: Die Tötung von Frauen durch ihre Partner oder Ex-Partner zieht bisher nicht durchgängig lebenslange Freiheitsstrafen nach sich. Bundesjustizministerin Hubig kämpft für eine »Klarstellung mit Signalwirkung«.

spiegel.title: Formel-1-Fahrer Charles Leclerc: Nur eine kleine Berührung - Haltungsnote
spiegel.description: Zwei Fahrer im selben Rennstall sind oft eher erbitterte Rivalen als Teamkollegen. Charles Leclerc wollte bei Ferrari nicht die Nummer zwei hinter Superstar Lewis Hamilton sein – und hat nun womöglich das Gegenteil erreicht.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump will Nvidia-Verwaltungsrat von Comeback von Jensen Huang überzeugt haben
spiegel.description: Jensen Huang ist zurück an der Spitze des Chipkonzerns Nvidia. Dafür sieht sich vor allem ein Mann als entscheidenden Faktor: US-Präsident Donald Trump. Doch die Aktion sorgt in den USA auch für heftige Kritik.

spiegel.title: Ratten lassen sich manipulieren, zeigt Studie aus Sydney
spiegel.description: Ähnlich wie Menschen lassen sich offenbar auch Ratten bei der Entscheidungsfindung beeinflussen, zeigt eine neue Studie aus Australien. Das könnte helfen, die Tiere in Fallen zu locken.

spiegel.title: Europäische Union will russische Flagge bei Sportveranstaltungen verbieten
spiegel.description: Brüssel will Staatssymbole Russlands von den Spielfeldern verbannen. Das würde Verbänden im Angesicht von Boykottdrohungen aus Mitgliedstaaten die Entscheidung abnehmen. Der Vorstoß ist Teil des neuen Sanktionspakets.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Nuklearwaffen im All, Jensen Huang ist wieder Nvdia-Chef, Markus Söder stichelt
spiegel.description: Nvidia holt den gerade erst zurückgetretenen Jensen Huang zurück. Russland könnte einen Atomsprengkopf ins Weltall befördern. Und Bayern bekommt einen neuen Söder-Stellvertreter. Das ist die Lage am Montagabend.

spiegel.title: Nato-Treffen in Berlin: Friedrich Merz und Mark Rutte bekräftigen Sicherheitsgarantien für die Ukraine
spiegel.description: Der Bundeskanzler und der Nato-Generalsekretär fordern Sicherheitsgarantien für die Ukraine. Diese würden einem Bündnisbeitritt sehr nahekommen, gelobt Merz. Er äußerte sich auch zu den in Polen abgestürzten Marschflugkörpern.

spiegel.title: Jensen Huang: Spionage-Affäre, Aktieneinbruch, Rückkehr – der Nvidia-Skandal um seien Firmenchef
spiegel.description: Der US-Chipriese Nvidia holt überraschend seinen erst kürzlich zurückgetretenen Chef Jensen Huang zurück. Er stürzte über zwei Affären, eine der Frauen soll eine chinesische Spionin sein. Chronologie des Skandals.

spiegel.title: AfD: Bundesvorstand will Bochumer Bundestagsabgeordneten loswerden
spiegel.description: Der Machtkampf der AfD in Nordrhein-Westfalen eskaliert weiter. Nun soll der Bundestagsabgeordnete Knuth Meyer-Soltau die Partei verlassen. Die Personalie hängt zusammen mit der Aufstellung für die NRW-Landtagswahl 2027.

letemps.description:
Les conclusions du nouveau rapport publié lundi sur les destructions environnementales à Gaza pourraient s’ajouter aux accusations de crimes de guerre examinées par la justice internationale à l’encontre d’Israël, relève l’avocat Johann Soufi

letemps.description:
Une audience dense et éprouvante s’est déroulée ce lundi à Renens, où le conseiller national UDC comparaît pour lésions corporelles, contrainte, menaces et séquestration sur son ex-femme. letemps.description:

letemps.title: Stellantis arrête toutes les compétitions automobiles dont les 24 Heures du Mans et les Championnats du monde d’endurance
letemps.description:
Coup de tonnerre dans le sport automobile. Stellantis, la holding de Peugeot, Citroën et Opel, cessera d’ici à la fin 2027 toutes les compétitions. Pour faire des économies

letemps.title: Des documents internes de la FIFA ont été publiés à la suite d’une cyberattaque
letemps.description:
Des documents internes de la FIFA se sont retrouvés en ligne à la suite d’une cyberattaque menée par un nouveau groupe de hackers. Ils comprennent quelques précisions sur le projet de vente d’une partie des droits commerciaux de la Coupe du monde à des investisseurs

letemps.description:
A quelques mois de la fin de son mandat, le chef de l’Etat français mise sur Choose France et propose d’inscrire dans la Constitution une trajectoire pluriannuelle de retour à l’équilibre des finances publiques. Un moyen pour lui de défendre son action depuis 2017

letemps.description:
COMMENTAIRE. Nouveau rebondissement dans le feuilleton Nvidia: le géant des semi-conducteurs réintègre son patron évincé, mais ne rassure pas. Et face aux manœuvres de la Maison-Blanche, on se pince pour y croire

phys-org.title: A nearly 100-million-year-old hairy snail pays tribute to the Prodigy's lead singer
phys-org.description: Myanmar amber (more commonly known as "burmite") is one of the most important sources of information about biodiversity during the Mesozoic Era. This amber dates back to the age of the dinosaurs and is approximately 99 million years old. Burmite preserves numerous now-extinct organisms (animals, plants, fungi, etc.) as inclusions, often in astonishing detail. This is because amber can preserve even soft tissues, which would otherwise decompose rapidly, and do so in three dimensions.

phys-org.title: A cactus that changes gears: How the prickly pear makes the most of desert rain
phys-org.description: In the desert, water doesn't arrive steadily. It comes in short pulses: a winter storm, a few rainy days, then months of drought. A desert plant needs two skills to live there. It has to survive the long dry spells, and it has to make full use of the brief windows when water is plentiful. A new study from Ben-Gurion University of the Negev and the Volcani Institute shows that the prickly pear cactus has an unexpected way of doing both.

phys-org.title: Overlooked symmetry group offers new geometric blueprint for the Standard Model and topologically protected vacuums
phys-org.description: For more than half a century, physicists searching for a grand unified theory have followed one unspoken rule: go bigger. If you want to weave nature's fundamental forces into a single mathematical framework, the classic recipe says you need a giant "simple" symmetry group—structures like SU(5) or SO(10) that act like massive algebraic warehouses large enough to hold every force at once.

phys-org.title: A hidden link between a flower's color and its scent revealed
phys-org.description: Researchers discovered that the biological machinery behind flower color also helps shape fragrance. By disrupting a single gene in petunias, they changed the flowers' mix of scent compounds, increasing some associated with vanilla and cloves.

phys-org.title: South Africa's small cattle farmers need help before super El Niño hits: How to set up shade, water and feed
phys-org.description: In South Africa, more than 2 million smallholder households make a living through agriculture. Within this small-scale farming sector, roughly 613,000 families own cattle. They farm on shared rural rangelands.

phys-org.title: Nanoparticles repair mitochondria to boost bone regeneration in diabetic rats
phys-org.description: A complication of diabetes is that damaged bones don't heal well, but a group of researchers is helping solve the problem with a novel mechanism to help bone regeneration.

phys-org.title: Webb finds evidence star's layers may have merged just hours before Cas A supernova
phys-org.description: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has painted a vibrant tapestry of the legendary supernova remnant Cassiopeia A (Cas A). Remnants like these are the clouds of gas and dust that remain following the explosion of a massive star and will eventually seed a new generation of stars and planets.

phys-org.title: Bacteria and nuclear power could grow ready-made homes on Mars before astronauts arrive
phys-org.description: As we gear up to eventually land a human on Mars, more and more ideas are coming out about how to prepare for that. A recent one from Pioneer Labs, a research institute founded by bioengineer Erika DeBenedictis to develop biological technologies for space exploration, is now available on the arXiv preprint server, without any plans to release it in a paid journal as part of the "Open Science" policy of The Astera Institute.

phys-org.title: Hera surveys asteroids with superhuman vision
phys-org.description: The European Space Agency's Hera mission for planetary defense surveys its target asteroids with a combination of instruments, peering beyond the limits of the human eye. The larger Didymos asteroid—dominated by its dramatic equatorial ridge—is seen here from just 28.5 km (17.7 miles) away, variously in visible light, multispectral and thermal infrared vision.

phys-org.title: Data center policy review reveals 'chaotic' patchwork of rules across all 50 states
phys-org.description: The artificial intelligence boom has brought with it debates about where the data centers that run the technology will be located, how big they will be and how to ensure communities benefit from them. Underlying these debates is the question of whether state and local governments should ban them outright, welcome them with open arms or choose something in between.

phys-org.title: Satellite observations show how rain breaks up Earth's natural sunshades
phys-org.description: Delivering on its promise, the European Space Agency's EarthCARE satellite is already yielding new insights into the role that clouds play in regulating Earth's climate. The latest findings shed light on one of the processes that leads to the breakup of vast, bright cloud formations that help keep our planet cool—with rain emerging as a key driver.

phys-org.title: Some people claim to speak many languages. But what does it really mean to be a polyglot?
phys-org.description: Roughly half of the world's population speaks more than one language. But speaking two or three languages is very different from claiming proficiency in five, 10 or more.

phys-org.title: Reparations can work when claims are grounded in solid evidence
phys-org.description: At the Commonwealth summit in Antigua in November 2026, Britain's King Charles expressed sorrow for Britain's role in the slave trade.

phys-org.title: Stellar pulses reveal hidden binary in JWST calibration star sample
phys-org.description: Stars used to calibrate the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) must have precisely characterized spectra so that their fluxes can be measured accurately. Yet some stars that appear single may in fact harbor unresolved companions that alter their predicted radiation. One such object, HD 158485—an A-type star in the JWST calibration program—has now been shown to be a binary system whose two stars both pulsate.

phys-org.title: Which pollen is found in honey? Automated analysis closely matches conventional testing
phys-org.description: Pure rapeseed honey—or not quite? Single-flower honeys must contain a certain proportion of pollen from the respective plant. This is assessed by pollen analysis, which is time-consuming and requires specialist expertise. As part of a collaborative project, a research team from the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research (UFZ) and the German Centre for Integrative Biodiversity Research (iDiv) in Leipzig worked with several partners to develop an automated, AI-based pollen analysis method for

phys-org.title: Discovery of curse ritual in trash dump surprises Egyptologist: 'It must have been widespread in ancient Egypt'
phys-org.description: The discovery of 40 charred papyrus fragments at a temple in the ancient city of Thebes is changing researchers' understanding of one of ancient Egypt's most famous curse rituals. The fragments show that the ritual was probably far more widespread and commonplace than previously believed.

phys-org.title: A fungus that can survive in Chernobyl could help create materials that trap and break down nerve agents and pesticides
phys-org.description: Deep inside the Chernobyl exclusion zone, where radiation levels have remained unsafe for people for the past 40 years, black molds climb the walls of the damaged former nuclear plant in Ukraine. They're entirely undeterred by the radiation—in fact, some fungi even grow toward it.

phys-org.title: Super El Niño will add to Africa's heat crisis—how governments can protect people before it peaks
phys-org.description: The super El Niño developing in the Pacific is expected to strengthen toward the end of 2026 and persist into early 2027. It's set to intensify dangerous heat and cause severe drought across parts of Africa. This is likely to mean more heat-related illness and deaths, worsening water shortages and greater disruption to electricity, food supplies and essential services.

undark.title: Australia’s Social Media Ban Has Not Worked — For Now
undark.description: New data coming out of Australia suggests that bans alone may not be an effective enough deterrent to stop children from using social media. But the research faces limitations. What does that mean for other countries considering similar restrictions?

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing
undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

proj-syn.title: The Achilles’ Heel of Emerging Economies’ Trade
proj-syn.description: New research shows that 23% of global goods imports in 2024 faced at least two of three vulnerabilities: product criticality, supply concentration, and geopolitical distance. Given the wide range of problems, early diagnosis and targeted action are particularly important for emerging economies with limited fiscal space.

proj-syn.title: AI Agents Could Make Big Tech Bigger
proj-syn.description: The rise of agentic AI could give a handful of Big Tech firms unprecedented power over our personal lives. Unless lawmakers and regulators act now, these digital gatekeepers could manipulate consumers, turbocharge corporate surveillance, and threaten our individual rights and civil liberties.

proj-syn.title: If the AI Bubble Is Bursting, the Fallout Will Be Severe
proj-syn.description: With the S&P 500 following the tech-heavy NASDAQ into correction territory, even as Anthropic set a record with its initial public offering, this is a good moment to compare AI stock valuations with earlier asset-price bubbles. A look back at the dot-com boom and bust of the late 1990s offers ample cause for concern.

proj-syn.title: Journalism Can Be More Than AI Fodder
proj-syn.description: As AI fundamentally alters the information environment, news publishers risk becoming little more than content suppliers for Big Tech. To avoid that fate, many are drawing on their archives and expertise to develop AI tools that allow them to operate and compete on their own terms.

proj-syn.title: Governing African Economies as They Are
proj-syn.description: Africa cannot overcome its development challenges by applying the same knowledge, economic, and innovation systems that helped create them. Imagining and governing new ways forward will require three intellectual ruptures.

proj-syn.title: Making Earth Cool Again
proj-syn.description: Climate multilateralism is evolving into a two-tiered system in which high-level negotiations toward shared commitments and the real-world implementation of climate solutions become more mutually supportive. Only by unleashing such virtuous cycles can we keep the 1.5ºC target for global warming within reach.

proj-syn.title: America’s Lame-Duck Autocrat
proj-syn.description: When autocrats suffer a defeat, they tend to double down, such as by intensifying repression at home or behaving more recklessly abroad. With two years left in office after historic midterm election losses, this is the road US President Donald Trump appears to be taking.

proj-syn.title: Getting Ukraine’s House in Order
proj-syn.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly opposed the idea of forming a national unity government. But bringing opposition leaders into the cabinet would ensure the checks on corruption and wayward bureaucratic action that Zelensky’s team can no longer provide.

proj-syn.title: What Adam Smith Missed
proj-syn.description: For all that he got right, the "founding father" of economics failed to see how technological innovations lead to market monopolization. If AI is left to the invisible hand, it will almost certainly increase economic and political inequality, causing even deeper social polarization and further undermining democracy.

proj-syn.title: China Ratchets Up Its Weaponization of Trade
proj-syn.description: Just as the US has been leveraging its large market and technological leadership for geopolitical ends, China is now using its dominance in critical minerals, industrial inputs, and specialized manufacturing machinery to coerce and punish other countries. The consequences, both economic and geopolitical, are far-reaching.

proj-syn.title: There Is Only One Thing to Talk About With Russia
proj-syn.description: The European security order’s foundational principle is never to tolerate aggression. There is no need to revise that order, as the Kremlin has proposed, only to wait for a Russian regime that is willing to respect other countries’ territorial integrity and uphold its own previous commitments.

proj-syn.title: The Truth About Global AI Governance
proj-syn.description: Because the current approach to global AI governance presumes that developing countries are full of eager adopters of AI who need to be cautioned about the technology's risks, it overlooks what their information environments and media markets actually need. A survey of researchers who study 71 countries sets the record straight.

proj-syn.title: Demography is the Achilles’ Heel of Dictatorships
proj-syn.description: Governments that manipulate population figures often end up deceiving themselves as much as the public. When autocratic leaders mistake inflated numbers for real national strength, they make costly strategic mistakes and fail to address their countries’ demographic decline until it is too late.

proj-syn.title: The Silver Lining of a Data-Center Slowdown
proj-syn.description: With leading AI labs under intense competitive pressure to keep advancing the frontier of the technology's capabilities, resistance to the build-out of computing resources is not such a bad thing. The more time we can buy, the greater our chances of maximizing the potential benefits and mitigating the risks.

proj-syn.title: What Nvidia’s Crisis Reveals About the Chip War
proj-syn.description: Export restrictions, like those depriving China of Nvidia’s most advanced chips, may buy time by curtailing a competitor's access to frontier capabilities made elsewhere. But in any technological conflict, policymakers must remember that slowing a rival is not the same as strengthening oneself.

proj-syn.title: When Export Restraints Are the Lesser Evil
proj-syn.description: Governments face pressure to protect domestic industries while preserving access to cheaper foreign goods. The recent EU-China car-export deal offers an uneasy compromise that protects European automakers while keeping Chinese cars available to consumers, making it preferable to prohibitive tariffs.

proj-syn.title: The Trade Losses That Nobody Counts
proj-syn.description: While much of the United Kingdom’s post-Brexit debate has focused on the monetary value of lost trade with the European Union, the composition of UK-EU trade flows warrants closer attention. A sharp decline in the variety of products shipped to Europe suggests that the economic costs have been greater than many realize.

proj-syn.title: Nigeria’s Big Bet on Health Care
proj-syn.description: Nigeria’s dependence on imported medicines and medical equipment leaves families exposed to exchange-rate fluctuations and hospitals at the mercy of global supply chains. Expanding domestic manufacturing is essential to reducing the cost of treatment and ensuring that more Nigerians can access quality care.

crunchbase.title: 5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: Reflecting Sunlight From Space, Better Breathing And Smarter Garbage Trucks
crunchbase.description: What if solar farms could keep generating electricity after sunset with a little help from mirrors orbiting Earth? Or researchers could send an experiment into space for less than the price of a car? Our latest roundup also includes a company bringing AI to the old-school business of garbage hauling, another rethinking how factories are programmed, and a consumer brand betting that better breathing could become a big business.

crunchbase.title: What The Telecom Bust Taught Me About AI’s Debt Boom
crunchbase.description: The AI buildout’s growing reliance on debt echoes the telecom bubble, raising the risk that infrastructure spending will outpace the revenue needed to meet fixed repayment obligations. According to guest author David Spreng of Runway Growth Capital, even if AI fulfills its technological promise, borrowers’ survival will depend on realistic demand forecasts and debt tied to dependable cash flows, with missed timelines potentially forcing restructurings and bankruptcies.

crunchbase.title: The Blue Economy: The World’s Quietest Economic Engine And Its Smartest Cities
crunchbase.description: The $2.6 trillion blue economy is creating startup opportunities in maritime automation, clean energy and logistics, with blue tech funding nearing $10 billion through Q3 2026, driven largely by major defense deals. Alberto Onetti, chairman of Mind the Bridge, writes that ports are emerging as hubs for testing and scaling these technologies, but realizing their potential requires coordination among port authorities, startups, investors and policymakers.

crunchbase.title: What’s Next For Recruiting, Job Hunting And HR? More AI, Of Course
crunchbase.description: So far this year, venture backers have poured close to $4 billion into an assortment of global companies focused on recruiting, finding jobs and streamlining processes associated with HR and payroll management, Crunchbase data shows. Not surprisingly, the vast majority are also incorporating a heavy dose of AI.

crunchbase.title: Public Markets Are Frequently Wrong. The SaaSpocalypse Shows Us Why
crunchbase.description: The “SaaSpocalypse” selloff and uneven recovery exposed public markets’ difficulty distinguishing software companies that benefit from AI from those it threatens, particularly as deeply embedded platforms retain competitive advantages. In this guest essay, Richard Anton, co-founder and general partner of Oxx, argues that this volatility distorts private transaction pricing, undermines confidence in public ownership and makes IPOs less appealing to founders.

crunchbase.title: Anthropic Closes Up 17% After Massive IPO
crunchbase.description: The offering promises to be the public market event of the season, with the Claude creator seeing investor demand for shares well in excess of its capital-raising goals.

crunchbase.title: The Key Numbers I’m Watching As Anthropic Makes Its IPO Debut
crunchbase.description: Just three years after launching with zero revenue, Anthropic brought in $17 billion and says more than 11,900 customers now spend at least $100,000 a year. But its IPO filing also reveals enormous computing commitments and big questions about balancing growth with risks.

crunchbase.title: What To Measure When ARR Isn’t Enough
crunchbase.description: AI companies’ hybrid subscription, usage and outcome-based pricing makes headline ARR figures an unreliable measure of predictable revenue, often obscuring differences in customer commitments and spending patterns. Guest author Kenza Zayani, an early-stage investor at RTP Global, warns that as these businesses seek growth capital, investors increasingly expect evidence of retention, expansion, revenue predictability and sustainable margins to assess the durability of growth.
